title: Lubricant R&D batch record
description: Batch-produced object: the landing point where recipe + process = product. A formula fixes intent and a trajectory records what the equipment actually did, so the batch record is the only place where setpoint-versus-actual deviations can be judged against the product that resulted. raw_material_lots is required because a batch is identified by the lots consumed, not by the trade names. anomalies may legitimately be empty ("none recorded") - that is a recorded absence, not missing data - while batch_verdict states whether the recorded trajectory is VALID, DEVIATED, or VOID.

formula_reference.description: Formula this batch was made from, together with the process baseline the formula requires.

trajectory.description: Ordered process steps actually executed, each with setpoint, actual, duration, and a per-step deviation verdict. Step types cover the grease route: saponification, dehydration, phase inversion, dilution/cooling, milling, homogenization, vacuum deaeration, filling, soap hold, dilution curve, ripening, filling temperature.

raw_material_lots.description: Lots charged into this batch. minItems 1: a batch with no recorded lot cannot be traced back to a material record.

anomalies.description: Anything unexpected observed during the batch. An empty array means "none recorded" and is a legitimate value, so no minItems is applied here.

trajectory_step.description: One executed process step. setpoint and actual accept a number or a string so a qualitative step (for example a visual phase inversion) stays recordable; deviation_verdict forces an explicit WITHIN / DEVIATED judgement per step instead of one batch-level summary.
